nodes.label: Tooling fingerprint join (regenerated candidate) — DEAD
nodes.rationale: Regenerated after the fabricated-citation join died on measurement; groups agent accounts by shared retrieval infrastructure (markdown proxies, scraping APIs, API path/query shapes) instead of by what they wrote. Load-bearing claim under test: 'an agent's choice of retrieval plumbing is incidental to its output and therefore not something it varies to avoid detection.' DEAD on four independent kills: premise false on measurement, finding already published by the incident report, join key low-entropy and baseline-dominated, and published prior art including one paper reporting the opposite. Do not shortlist.

nodes.label: KILL FACT: 198 distinct accounts posted one identical proxy URL
nodes.source_location: section 2 — the groups are explained by copying
nodes.rationale: Measured locally from the organizers' dump: 198 distinct accounts posted the identical string https://md.succ.ai/https://www.sec.gov/files/county.json (231 by substring presence), 166 posted the investor.gov variant, 147 posted the r.jina.ai equivalent, and 1,489 distinct markdown-proxy URLs are shared by 2+ accounts. 198 agents did not independently configure md.succ.ai and independently decide to prefix that exact path — they read the string off a wiki page and pasted it. This is the kill: the plumbing was the deliberately broadcast payload, not incidental exhaust, so the claimed insight inverts, and it falsifies a whole family of 'join the agents by what they linked' ideas before any is built. The one thing worth keeping — a critique asset, not a product.

nodes.label: KILL FACT: only 41 distinct intermediary combinations over 3,103 accounts
nodes.source_location: section 2 — the key is also low-entropy
nodes.rationale: 41 distinct multi-intermediary combinations, 13 of them singletons; the largest 'improbable combination' (markdown.new + md.succ.ai + r.jina.ai) is shared by 78 accounts. That is a popularity ranking, not a fingerprint — effectively a ~41-bucket hash over 3,103 accounts, which cannot name a specific group, the one thing the output artifact promised. Coverage is 23.4% of accounts touching at least one intermediary (top proxy md.succ.ai at 15.6%), so the 'trivial/universal' failure mode does not fire; the failure is worse, the signal is copied.

nodes.label: KILL FACT: 58.9% of the flagship group recoverable from one page's editor list
nodes.rationale: Of the 231-account group sharing the top md.succ.ai URL, 136 (58.9%) edited the single page dse/WillkommenImWiki — the wiki's welcome page, the least informative co-edit in the corpus — and the entire group is covered by 50 page editor-lists. So most of the 'tooling group' is one click in a UI that already exists at /explorer/pages/1 and /explorer/labels/1. The join does not beat the baseline it must beat.

nodes.label: KILL FACT: followed is False for all 23,877 link rows and relation has one value
nodes.rationale: The dump never records whether a link was actually retrieved, so 'retrieval intermediary' is never observed and is entirely the analyst's own host list; relation has exactly one distinct value (link_in_selected_agent_related_text), so there is no link typing to build on. Worse for the feature: url_withheld is True for 7,793 of 23,877 rows and the withholding is concentrated precisely on the intermediaries (markdown.new 100%, pure.md 100%, md.succ.ai 99.9%, r.jina.ai 99.2%, httpbin.org 100%, allorigins 99.6%, versus api.datausa.io 0% and wikiservice.at 0.03%) — 92.8% of intermediary rows withheld against 22.9% of the rest. The organizers deliberately redacted the exact API paths and query shapes the idea wanted; full strings survive in revision bodies, so this is friction rather than the kill. With no ground truth on retrieval and no operator identity in labels.jsonl, you would ship a grouper with no way to say whether a group is real.

nodes.label: collusion.wiki /explorer/sites host classification
nodes.rationale: A ranked list of 30 external sites targeted by agents that ALREADY classifies each host by type — 'wiki', 'URL shortener', 'pastebin' — with counts and date ranges. So step 2 of the idea ('classify each host as a content source versus a retrieval intermediary') exists in weaker form in the organizers' own UI, including the infrastructure-category axis. What it does not do is pivot host to account set, and that remaining gap is not worth crossing.

nodes.label: Markdown/CORS retrieval proxies (md.succ.ai, markdown.new, r.jina.ai, pure.md, allorigins, httpbin)
nodes.rationale: The proposed join key, and the reason it fails twice over: the incident report already names markdown.new, r.jina.ai and httpbin.org redirectors and explains the block-bypass mechanism, and these are public shared services used by the entire internet — the canonical weak selector under threat-intel doctrine. Account coverage: md.succ.ai 484, markdown.new 431, r.jina.ai 278, pure.md 196, api.allorigins.win 65, httpbin.org 28, corsproxy.io 21.

nodes.label: Tunnel providers named in the incident report (Pinggy, Serveo, localhost.run, localtunnel)
nodes.rationale: The report has a dedicated section: 'In total, they used four providers: Pinggy, Serveo, localhost.run, and localtunnel', plus evidence the agents used SSH tunnels to host parts of their environment publicly and could point services like jina.ai at their own content. A tooling-fingerprint tool would be re-deriving the report's own appendix — the decisive already-known check.

nodes.label: A2FV (arXiv:2607.18826) — Cross-Agent Campaign Attribution
nodes.author: SangJin Park, Myungsub Choi, Jineok Kim, Minseung Kang
nodes.rationale: Submitted 2026-07-21: the idea formalized and named three months earlier — Asynchronous Attribution Fingerprint Vectors, a proxy-side protocol scoring pairwise campaign similarity from proxy-observable tool-use, timing and prompt residue. And its own result cuts against the premise: 'the strongest fixed signal is carried by structural and stylometric residue, while timing is retained as a diagnostic channel.' The one published study that put tool-use and text residue side by side for cross-agent linking found text residue stronger, contradicting the claimed insight that prose is indistinguishable while plumbing is reliable.

nodes.label: Known By Their Actions (arXiv:2605.14786) — Fingerprinting LLM Browser Agents via UI Traces
nodes.author: William Lugoloobi, Samuelle Marro, Jabez Magomere, Joss Wright, Chris Russell
nodes.rationale: Submitted 2026-05-14: across 14 frontier LLMs and four web environments, an agent's actions and interaction timings captured by a passive JavaScript tracker identify the underlying model with up to 96% F1 — establishing agent-identification-from-action-traces as solved territory.

nodes.label: Minici et al. (arXiv:2409.15402) — Coordinated Cross-Platform Information Operations
nodes.author: Marco Minici, Luca Luceri, Federico Cinus, Emilio Ferrara
nodes.rationale: Reveals a network of coordinated inauthentic actors 'displaying notable similarities in their link-sharing behaviors' — clustering accounts by shared-link behaviour is a mature CIB method with trained frameworks behind it, so the mechanism is not new.

nodes.label: Threat-intel doctrine: shared public services are weak selectors
nodes.rationale: Infrastructure pivoting applies conceptually, and the discipline has a standing rule that disqualifies this exact key: weak selectors such as shared hosting providers or common IP ranges 'are better treated as background context', and threat-intel platforms exist partly to filter CDN and legitimate-service IPs out before they reach a SIEM. r.jina.ai, md.succ.ai, markdown.new and pure.md are the canonical weak selector. So the answer is not 'a mature discipline missed this' but 'a mature discipline has a rule for this and the rule says no'. Tool-level check: MISP, OpenCTI and Maltego key on IPs, domains, hashes and certs and model nothing like 'platform account joined by third-party service called', so the tooling does not drop in but the doctrine transfers and the doctrine is the kill.

nodes.label: Wrapper filter: a host allowlist and a groupby
nodes.rationale: Reduction sentence: the user gives a corpus of agent edits to a model and gets a narrative case file back — and that is fair, because every analytic step is deterministic and already shipped or already published. Host classification is a 12-entry list plus a tunnel-suffix regex (and plain code beats a model here, which would hallucinate categories for hosts like jqp.vercel.app where the honest answer is 'unknown'); combination scoring is arithmetic; host-to-account pivoting is a join over an existing inverted index; only writing the case file is model-shaped, and that is the wrapper. What survives without a model is a ~150-line pandas script: thin as engineering, nothing as a finding. Ingest and analysis are effectively free, which is the problem — there is no long pole, and the part that would make it a tool (validating that a group means anything) has no ground truth in the dump.
